title: Find Minimum In Rotated Sorted Array
description: A sorted array of **unique** integers was rotated between 1 and `n` times (one rotation moves the last element to the front). Given the rotated array `nums`, return its minimum element. Your algorithm must run in O(log n) time.
hints: A linear scan is O(n). The array has structure: it is two sorted runs joined together.
Compare nums[mid] with nums[right]. What does nums[mid] > nums[right] tell you about where the drop is?
If nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum is in (mid, right]; otherwise it is at mid or to its left, so set right = mid. Stop when left == right.

solution.explanation: Binary search on the rotation point. If nums[mid] is greater than nums[right], the drop (and the minimum) lies strictly right of mid, so move left to mid + 1. Otherwise the right part is sorted and the minimum is at mid or earlier, so set right = mid. The range shrinks by half each step, ending on the minimum: O(log n) time, O(1) space.
